title: CNMC Goldmine shares plunge as gold falls below US$4,000
html:
Shares of CNMC Goldmine are down nearly 30% in the past month.

PHOTO: CNMC GOLDMINE

Timothy Goh

SINGAPORE – Shares of CNMC Goldmine Holdings plunged on Nov 16, extending recent losses as gold prices dipped below US$4,000 an ounce following a sell-off in the precious metal.

The mainboard-listed mining stock sank nearly 11% to 85 cents at the midday trading break on Nov 16, bringing its losses to about 20.56% over the past five trading sessions and almost 30% over the past month.

About 5.5 million shares changed hands during the morning trading session on Nov 16.

Spot gold, meanwhile, fell 0.24% to US$3,872 (S$4,990) an ounce, as signs that the US Federal Reserve could raise rates weighed on sentiment. This came ahead of remarks by Fed chair Kevin Warsh at a Nov 16 US conference that could offer further clues on the direction of interest rates.

Gold has fallen nearly 6% since the start of the year, as elevated US Treasury yields and a stronger greenback dampened demand for the precious metal.

Hashim Osman, a research analyst at Phillip Securities Research, attributed CNMC’s share price decline to growing expectations of further US interest rate hikes.

This follows stronger-than-expected inflation data last week and consensus among Fed officials that inflation remains too high.

“In this environment, the key differentiator among miners is their ability to limit margin erosion as gold prices ease,” he said.

Elevated fuel costs remain a concern for investors, particularly for miners investing in exploration and development, he added.

CNMC’s net profit rose 17.8% to US$18.6 million for the six months ended June 30, 2026, from US$15.8 million a year earlier.

The Singapore-headquartered gold and base metals producer, which operates in Kelantan, Malaysia, generated US$65.2 million in revenue for first half of 2026, up 23.4% from a year earlier, driven by higher gold, silver and zinc prices.

Revenue from gold produced at its carbon-in-leach plant at its flagship Sokor mine increased 32% to US$49.8 million.

Revenue from gold produced at its flagship Sokor mine’s carbon-in-leach plant rose 32% to US$49.8 million, even as production fell 6% to 11,105 ounces.

Including gold produced from lead concentrate at its flotation plant, which is used primarily to recover base metals, the company generated total revenue of US$56.7 million from gold in the first half of 2026, a 27.4% increase from a year earlier.

Still, CNMC’s all-in production cost is about US$2000 per ounce, so margins would still be intact even if gold retreats further.
summary: Spot gold fell 0.24% to US$3,872 an ounce on Nov 16.
